content.value_statement: Engineering leaders need consistent ways to assess debt, scale teams, and choose technologies. This skill provides CTO-ready frameworks, calculators, templates, and metrics guidance for structured technical leadership decisions.
actual_capabilities: Assess technical debt across architecture, code quality, infrastructure, security, and performance categories.
Generate team scaling plans with hiring priorities, quarterly growth timelines, and budget projections.
Provide architecture decision record templates and examples for major technical choices.
Compare technologies and vendors with weighted technical, business, and operational criteria.
Define engineering metrics using DORA, quality, velocity, team health, and OKR frameworks.
Draft communication templates for strategy presentations, all-hands meetings, and board updates.
limitations: Calculators use generic assumptions and example inputs unless users provide their own data.
The skill does not connect to Jira, GitHub, observability tools, or HR systems automatically.
Recommendations need validation against company finances, regulatory duties, and local labor markets.
It supports planning and analysis, not final executive approval or legal advice.

use_cases.title: Plan Engineering Growth
use_cases.description: Create a hiring sequence, role mix, budget estimate, and team structure for a scaling engineering organization.

use_cases.title: Build Metrics Governance
use_cases.description: Select DORA, quality, delivery, and team health metrics with safeguards against metric gaming.

use_cases.title: Document Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Use ADR templates to compare options, record trade-offs, and communicate decisions to stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Technical Debt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a quick debt review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our main application for technical debt. Ask me for architecture, code quality, infrastructure, security, and performance details before recommending priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Create Team Scaling Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a team scaling plan from our current engineering team to our target headcount. Include role gaps, quarterly hiring, budget risks, and onboarding constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Technology Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me evaluate three technology options for a critical platform decision. Score technical, business, and operational criteria, then summarize trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CTO Operating Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced executive review across strategy and execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a CTO operating review covering technical debt, engineering metrics, architecture decisions, hiring risks, vendor strategy, and next-quarter priorities.

output_examples.input: Assess technical debt for a legacy commerce platform with weak tests and manual deployments.
output: Overall debt level: medium-high, with security and infrastructure as top risks.
Recommended focus: CI/CD automation, vulnerability scanning, and test coverage gates.
Suggested capacity: dedicate 25 percent of sprint capacity for two quarters.

output_examples.input: Plan growth from 25 to 75 engineers over four quarters.
output: Hiring should emphasize engineering managers, tech leads, senior engineers, and DevOps capacity first.
Main risks are onboarding load, communication overhead, and culture dilution.
A phased structure with platform, product, infrastructure, and data teams is recommended.

output_examples.input: Create an ADR for choosing Kubernetes over ECS and Nomad.
output: Decision context: microservices need automated deployment, scaling, and high availability.
Chosen option: Kubernetes, because of ecosystem maturity and multi-cloud portability.
Consequences: higher operational complexity, mitigated through managed Kubernetes and training.

best_practices: Provide current metrics, team size, business goals, and constraints before asking for recommendations.
Use the calculators as planning aids, then validate assumptions with finance, HR, and engineering leads.
Pair every architecture or vendor recommendation with an ADR and a measurable success metric.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic salary, velocity, or team ratio assumptions as final operating plans.
Do not optimize one metric without checking quality, reliability, and team health impacts.
Do not treat framework output as a substitute for stakeholder alignment and risk review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps leaders assess technical debt, scale teams, document architecture choices, evaluate technologies, and define engineering metrics.

faq.question: Can it run calculations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes local Python calculators for technical debt analysis and engineering team scaling examples.

faq.question: Does it connect to live engineering tools?
faq.answer: No. It does not automatically pull data from source control, ticketing, observability, finance, or HR systems.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It is useful for CTOs, VPs of Engineering, engineering managers, staff engineers, and technical program leaders.

faq.question: Can it choose a vendor for me?
faq.answer: It can structure the evaluation and score options, but final selection needs business, legal, security, and procurement review.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
